hints: Look first at what functional groups the three IR spectra actually show, especially any C=O peak near 1700 and any broad O-H absorption.
Product Y has a strong sharp C=O peak but no broad O-H, while product Z has both a C=O peak and a very broad absorption from 2500 to 3500 cm-1.
Think of oxidative cleavage of a C=C bond, where a trisubstituted alkene can split to give one ketone fragment and one carboxylic acid fragment.
walkthrough:
**Read spectrum X**

Reactant X shows only strong absorptions just below 3000 cm-1 for C-H bonds. There is no broad O-H band and no C=O band near 1700 cm-1, so X is a hydrocarbon, not an oxygen-containing compound.

Rule: $\text{C=O} \approx 1680-1750 \text{ cm}^{-1}$, $\text{O-H (acid)} \approx 2500-3500 \text{ cm}^{-1}$ broad

**Read spectrum Y**

Product Y shows a very strong sharp dip at about 1715 cm-1 for C=O, plus C-H near 3000 cm-1, but no broad O-H absorption. That is characteristic of a ketone, not a carboxylic acid or alcohol.

Rule: ketone = $\text{C=O}$ present, $\text{O-H}$ absent

**Read spectrum Z**

Product Z shows both a strong C=O peak near 1710 cm-1 and a very broad, low transmittance band from about 2500 to 3500 cm-1. That broad band is the hydrogen-bonded O-H of a carboxylic acid.

Rule: carboxylic acid = $\text{C=O}$ present + very broad $\text{O-H}$ present

**Match to oxidative cleavage**

Hot concentrated $\text{KMnO}_4$ cleaves $\text{C=C}$: $\text{R}_2\text{C=CR}_2 \rightarrow$ ketones, $\text{RCH=}$ $\rightarrow$ carboxylic acids. For $\text{(CH}_3\text{)}_2\text{C=CHCH}_2\text{CH}_3$:
$$\text{(CH}_3\text{)}_2\text{C=CHCH}_2\text{CH}_3 \rightarrow \text{(CH}_3\text{)}_2\text{C=O} + \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COOH}$$
That is 2-methylpent-2-ene to propanone plus propanoic acid, which fits X = alkene, Y = ketone, Z = acid.

options.A: 2,3-dimethylpent-2-ene cleavage would give propanone plus butanone, two ketones. Both products would then show sharp C=O with no broad O-H, but spectrum Z clearly shows the broad O-H of a carboxylic acid, so this row fails.
options.B: 2-methylpent-2-ene has no O-H or C=O, matching X. Cleavage gives propanone, a ketone matching Y with sharp C=O and no broad O-H, and propanoic acid, matching Z with C=O plus very broad O-H. Atom balance also works: C6 alkene to C3 + C3 fragments.
options.C: Pent-2-ene cleavage would give two carboxylic acids, ethanoic acid and propanoic acid. Both Y and Z would then show the very broad acid O-H band, but spectrum Y has no broad O-H and is a ketone spectrum, so Y cannot be ethanoic acid.
options.D: Propyl propanoate is an ester and must show a strong C=O peak near 1735 cm-1, but spectrum X has no C=O peak. Also hydrolysis to propan-1-ol would give a narrower O-H band and no C=O in Y, but Y clearly has a strong C=O, so this row fails on both X and Y.
